analysis.title: GS Basics - Commodity Disinflation. Technicals. Hynix Multiple.
key_insights: Nvidia beat and raised overnight with a $130bn guide against roughly $125bn expected, and the guide includes zero China data center compute. Privorotsky reads this as spending on AI continuing. The one thing the market wanted was a hint that Jensen Huang could return to China, and the company shut that down.
Tech-related markets are recovering off the lows. Kospi is holding the lows of the prior selloff and is up 2%. SK Hynix trades at 1.79x blended 24-month P/E (Bloomberg).

Yesterday's tape: high beta momentum rose, AI stocks outperformed AI losers, and the short leg of momentum got hit. Expensive defensives that had gone too far fell alongside small and mid cap cyclicals. Privorotsky saw this as somewhat constructive from a gross positioning standpoint. Asia showed a similar pattern with Korea leading.

Cyber anxiety: Privorotsky thinks the market worried that the recent outages were connected, but WIRED reports no evidence that the clustered failures were related or caused by hackers. Costco had sold out of 21 of 26 high ticket generator models online by Sunday (Bloomberg), which he reads as panic buying and a sentiment signal. He expects cyber incidents to keep rising but thinks anxiety on the topic has hit a local peak.

APEC: Trump and Xi are due to meet Thursday in Shenzhen, with Putin reportedly joining a separate three way conversation. Privorotsky is watching whether the trade truce holds after the new US chip curbs, and is bearish on a near-term Russia/Ukraine ceasefire, citing reports that Ukraine took out the central road span of the Kerch Bridge two days before the meeting.

Oil: the US hit an Iranian missile launch site Tuesday after Iran said it targeted a US radar installation in Bahrain. Oman and Qatar are still talking to Tehran. Privorotsky sees obvious incentives for a deal nine months in, especially after the midterms, but no clear path.

The US 3-2-1 crack spread is down 36% in six weeks, from $65.56 to $41.90/bbl. Gasoline and diesel are weakening against crude even with Hormuz keeping a premium in Brent. API data showed US crude and gasoline stocks each building by about 5m barrels.

Metals: London copper is near 5m lows, Shanghai copper is testing 100k, and gold cannot hold a bounce even with some relief in yields. Privorotsky suggests a liquidation element in gold and says the China tape has been awful, possibly a sign that policy is too tight.

Technicals: the velocity of CTA selling may have peaked, but the magnitude can still be large if the market stays here, especially in Europe. Vol stabilizing matters for vol control funds, and spot gamma remains very level dependent. SPX is holding the 200-day moving average by a fingernail. Nasdaq broke its early month lows intraday and recovered them by the close.

Risk view: positioning was already defensive, so Privorotsky expected more chop. Outside of cyber he cannot point to a clear catalyst for the last two days. He is starting to turn contrarian on AI, noting the dollars still to be spent, how far multiples have fallen, and what investors pay for defensives.

Rates and commodities: declines across copper, crude, gasoline, diesel and parts of the grain complex would be a meaningful disinflationary impulse if they persist. Privorotsky says one day is not a trend and thinks commodity pass-through to inflation is overcomplicated. He likes long front end bonds alongside equities.

Side note: cheap stocks getting cheaper is a worry for earnings sustainability, but it is very difficult to press lower at current multiples. If the market is bearish on AI or growth, he suggests expressing it in other pockets, since the margin of safety in names like SK Hynix is now meaningful.

tension_points.bear_case: Haircut to 2028 and worries about a peak in 2029. Cheap stocks getting cheaper raises earnings sustainability concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Privorotsky does not name a specific level. He notes that one day is not a trend for the commodity-driven disinflation view.
